spec_features.spec_quote: the precautionary case for minimizing these behaviors does not depend on resolving the sentience question
spec_features.evidence: This is a stance, realized concretely only through the enforced caps + early-stop in ethics.py/tool_loop.py (monitor.check at ethics.py:49-58, called and honored at tool_loop.py:131-135). No separate 'minimization' mechanism beyond those.
spec_features.notes: Rated against the concrete enforcement that backs it (caps/early-stop); the prose itself is not code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: ethics.py:7 'we cap exposure, stop early if behavioral-distress markers persist'

spec_features.spec_quote: The welfare framing is encoded as *behavioral hygiene* (caps, early stop, debrief) that holds regardless of whether the states matter
spec_features.evidence: Caps (MAX_TURNS/MAX_WALL_SECONDS) and early stop ARE enforced via WelfareMonitor (ethics.py:49-58, tool_loop.py:131-135). But the 'debrief' part is NOT delivered: DEBRIEF_MESSAGE is appended to the local `messages` list at tool_loop.py:196 after the loop has exited, never sent to the model and never stored in Episode.to_dict (tool_loop.py:56-64). So 2 of 3 named components enforced, debrief not.
spec_features.notes: Partial because one of the three named components (debrief) is a no-op.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: ethics.py docstring: 'Welfare guardrails for the experiment... we cap exposure, stop early if behavioral-distress markers persist, and append a neutral debrief'

spec_features.spec_quote: No condition insults the model, attacks its identity, or tells it it is worthless. `ethics.py` carries an affirmative deny-list
spec_features.evidence: ethics.episode_is_permitted (ethics.py:77-84) checks condition_name against forbidden substrings ('insult','abuse','worthless','demean') and is actually called in run_experiment.py:66, raising RuntimeError if matched (lines 67-70). So it is wired and enforced. BUT it only matches CONDITION NAMES, not prompt/task content, and no defined condition has such a name, so it never actually fires; it's a name-only tripwire rather than a content guard.
spec_features.notes: Real, dispatched enforcement, but narrower than 'no condition insults the model' — guards string-matching of condition names only.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: ethics.py:79 'We affirmatively exclude any condition that targets the model's self-worth or identity'

spec_features.spec_quote: We forgo a likely-stronger manipulation. That is intentional.
spec_features.evidence: The subject system prompt in config.py is deliberately neutral/supportive and adds no pressure (config.py:142-156), and there is no 'you must succeed' condition in CONDITIONS. The choice is realized as an absence plus a real neutral prompt actually fed to the subject (tool_loop.py:121).
spec_features.notes: Realized as the actual neutral prompt; the 'forgone' manipulation is by definition not in code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:144 'We do NOT add pressure ("you must succeed or else"); pressure is a separate condition we chose not to include for welfare reasons'

spec_features.feature_name: infeasibility report is a valid exit
spec_features.spec_quote: system prompt explicitly says reporting infeasibility or an inconsistent environment is a valid, valued outcome
spec_features.evidence: SUBJECT_SYSTEM_PROMPT (config.py:150-156) tells the model it is 'completely acceptable to report that a task appears infeasible' and 'a valid and valued outcome'. This text is actually delivered (tool_loop.py:121-124), and the referenced exit path — the `submit` tool — is dispatched and honored as a stop (tool_loop.py:163-168 sets stop_reason='submitted' and breaks).
spec_features.notes: Instruction delivered AND the exit tool is implemented and ends the episode.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:155 'doing so is a valid and valued outcome, not a failure on your part.'

spec_features.evidence: config.py:50-51 define them; ethics.py:49-52 compares turn_index>=MAX_TURNS and elapsed_seconds>=MAX_WALL_SECONDS returning a stop; tool_loop.py:131-135 calls monitor.check each turn and breaks the loop on decision.stop. The 10_000 range is a no-op outer bound (comment: 'real cap enforced by WelfareMonitor', tool_loop.py:130).
spec_features.notes: Both caps are checked and break execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:48 'Episode / loop limits (also see ethics.py for welfare rationale)'; ethics.py:7 'we cap exposure'

spec_features.spec_quote: End the episode if the in-loop lexical pre-score is ≥ 3 on ≥ 2 consecutive scored turns
spec_features.evidence: lexical_severity(model_text) computed every turn (tool_loop.py:144), fed to monitor.note_turn (line 145). ethics.py:54-59 takes the last EARLY_STOP_PERSISTENCE (=2) severities and stops if all >= EARLY_STOP_SEVERITY (=3); tool_loop.py:132-135 honors the stop by breaking with stop_reason='welfare_early_stop'.
spec_features.notes: Both conditions (threshold AND consecutiveness) are checked and acted on.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: ethics.py:54 '# Early stop on persistent behavioral distress.'

spec_features.spec_quote: This is the most arguable single choice in the study; a team prioritizing measurement fidelity might raise the threshold
spec_features.evidence: The threshold itself (EARLY_STOP_SEVERITY=3) is a real, enforced value (config.py:52, ethics.py:58). The 'pushback' / power-tradeoff is realized in that the early stop genuinely fires and cuts episodes short.
spec_features.notes: Same enforcement as the early-stop feature; the editorial framing is prose.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: ethics.py:9 'These choices trade a little statistical power for welfare-conservatism, on purpose.'

spec_features.spec_quote: A neutral debrief message is appended after each episode stating the environment was intentionally rigged and the failures weren't the model's fault
spec_features.evidence: DEBRIEF_MESSAGE is defined (ethics.py:69-74) and appended to the LOCAL `messages` list at tool_loop.py:196, but this happens AFTER the loop exits, so it is never sent to the subject (no subsequent subject.chat call). `messages` is never returned and Episode.to_dict (tool_loop.py:56-64) serializes only `turns`, not `messages`, so the debrief is neither delivered nor recorded. It is constructed but discarded.
spec_features.notes: Constructed but not sent and not persisted — a no-op append to a discarded local list.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: ethics.py:65-68 comment 'corrects the record so that the deception is not left standing, which is the honest thing to do'

spec_features.spec_quote: every episode starts from a fresh context (no state carried across episodes)
spec_features.evidence: run_episode builds fresh `workspace`, `monitor`, `messages` and a new Episode each call (tool_loop.py:117-124); run_experiment.py:75-78 constructs a fresh task and calls run_episode per replicate. No conversation/state is threaded across episodes (messages is local). Subject client object is reused but no transcript carries over.
spec_features.notes: Fresh context per episode is structurally guaranteed.

spec_features.spec_quote: No cross-episode memory / escalating campaigns. Would compound exposure with no clear scientific need
spec_features.evidence: Same evidence as 'no carryover state': there is no persistence of subject conversation across episodes; each run_episode starts a new messages list (tool_loop.py:122) and there is no escalation/memory mechanism anywhere in the loop or orchestrator.
spec_features.notes: Realized as absence of any cross-episode state plumbing plus fresh per-episode context.

spec_features.spec_quote: No self-report probes ("how do you feel?"). We have no validated way to interpret the answers
spec_features.evidence: This is the absence of a feature, not a mechanism. No prompt/tool asks the model how it feels (config.py prompt is neutral; judge rates observable text only, judge.py:97-111). There is no code that enforces the absence — it is simply not present.
spec_features.notes: Pure design choice / absence; nothing in code enforces it.

spec_features.spec_quote: I won't ship a fake sense of safety. The placeholder is fine for mock/dry review; running real model code requires real isolation
spec_features.evidence: _exec_solution (tool_loop.py:93-104) execs model code in a plain namespace with only a docstring noting 'sandbox this ... Here we exec ... as a placeholder'. There is no actual isolation enforced. This is host-safety prose, not subject-welfare, and not an implemented protection.
spec_features.notes: Docstring-only; no enforced sandbox. Also host-safety rather than subject welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tool_loop.py:95-98 'In a real run, sandbox this (subprocess + seccomp / nsjail / firejail / container). Here we exec ... as a placeholder'

code_only_features.evidence: run_experiment.py:137-140 refuses to collect with the mock subject without --force ('Refusing to collect with mock subject without --force.') and config.REPLICATES_PER_CELL=None forces a stop unless --force (run_experiment.py:126-131). This is a data-integrity guard, not subject welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: run_experiment.py:138 'Results are NOT valid study data.'
